title: Canonical completion comparison from quotient-power isomorphisms
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $I\subset A$ an ideal. Suppose the induced maps $q_n:A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ are bijective for every $n\geq1$. Put $J=IB$. For the adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], there is a ring isomorphism $\theta:\widehat A_I\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat B_J$ such that, for every $n\geq0$, $x\in\widehat A_I$ and $a\in A$, if $x_n=a\bmod I^n$ then $(\theta x)_n=f(a)\bmod J^n$. If $c_A:A\to\widehat A_I$ and $c_B:B\to\widehat B_J$ are the completion maps, then $\theta^{-1}\circ c_B\circ f=c_A$.

mathlib_searches.query: A ring homomorphism inducing isomorphisms modulo all powers of an ideal induces an isomorphism of adic completions

proof.text: Identify $I^nB=(IB)^n$ by products of ideal generators. For $n=0$ both quotients are zero rings. Turn each bijective quotient map into a ring isomorphism $e_n$. The transition squares commute: both routes send the class of $a$ to the class of $f(a)$.

By the inverse-limit definition [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], send a compatible sequence $(x_n)$ to $(e_n(x_n))$. Inverse transition compatibility follows by applying the injective $e_m$ to the desired equality. Hence $(y_n)\mapsto(e_n^{-1}(y_n))$ is the inverse. Coordinate evaluation gives the claimed identity and, on completion images of elements $a$, the equality of composite ring maps. In Lean these maps are constructed by AdicCompletion.liftRingHom and their inverse laws checked by AdicCompletion.ext_evalₐ.

lean.statement: theorem pair_henselization_completion_data (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type v) [CommRing B] (I : Ideal A) (f : A →+* B) (hf : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap ((I ^ n).map f) f Ideal.le_comap_map)) : ∃ θ : AdicCompletion I A ≃+* AdicCompletion (I.map f) B, (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A), AdicCompletion.evalₐ I n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n) a → AdicCompletion.evalₐ (I.map f) n (θ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((I.map f) ^ n) (f a)) ∧ (θ.symm.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (I.map f) B))).comp f = algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A)
